newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in commercial market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in commercial market.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.03 percent to close at 1.0591 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market as the Central Bank lowered the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank adjusted the mini-band downward 0.09 percent to a range between 1.0590 and 1.0640 reais per dollar.

Analysts said the real's drop less than that of the mini-band adjustment for two reasons: firstly, the market had already traded the real near of the new level on Thursday, when the local currency closed at 1.0588 per greenback.
Secondly, some banks decided to sell dollar holdings, increasing the supply of dollars in the market.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.19 percent against the dollar against an average drop of between 0.5 and 0.6 percent in the past four months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real fell 0.13 percent to end at 1.0665 per greenback due to a reduction in the supply of dollars.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.44 percent, closing at 1.125 per dollar, traders said.
